newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses slide, depressed by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses slide, depressed by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses slipped on Thursday with nervous investors depressed by an overnight fall on Wall Street ahead of U.S. inflation figures this week.

The dollar was little changed from late Wednesday's levels as foreign exchange traders awaited Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer price data that will provide pointers to interest rate prospects.
London stocks dipped in early trading after a sharp decline on Thursday ended a four-day run of record closes. Wall Street's 36-point drop contributed to the gloom in European markets.
"I don't think the market will have as bad a performance as as yesterday. Underneath this market, there's still a bit of money around that wants to get in on the dips," said one trader.

London's bull run and the surge in other European bourses have been fuelled by signs the U.S. economy, after rapid expansion, is slowing to a level where it can sustain inflation-free growth and low interest rates.
Any change in this scenario would be regarded as bad news by markets. Hence investors are apprehensive about the release of U.S. wholesale inflation data for September.
"With the exception of higher petrol prices, it's difficult to see a significant acceleration in inflation," the trader said.

The U.S. central bank has held interest rates steady, but in Britain Bank of England governor Eddie George has been warning that British rates should be raised to dampen inflationary pressures, and that the longer the move is delayed, the more rates will need to be raised in the future.

Other European bourses were depressed by the decline in New York stocks, which skidded to their biggest loss in a month on the inflation worries. Wall Street also used an unfounded rumour that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had died as an excuse to take profits.
Frankfurt suffered the sharpest fall, dropping more than 0.6 percent amid depression over Wall Street.
French shares fell by 0.5 percent after opening in negative ground and traders said the market needed a pause to gain its breath after recent advances.
Trading was quiet as the CAC index slipped 11.21 to 2,135.50. Analysts said the index could consolidate around 2,100 before attacking the pyschologically important 2,200 level next week.
The dollar was virtually unchanged in quiet trading and forex dealers said they expected the current levels to remain at least until Friday's U.S. data.
"With nothing out of Japan the dollar/yen drifted lower, hitting stops at 111.30, but bids near 111 are providing support," said one European bank dealer.
The mark was stronger against European currencies in early trading ahead of Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting, which analysts said was unlikely to result in any change in rates.
Dealers said the overall firmer tone for the mark was likely to push the dollar to the lower reaches of its trading range. In early trading the dollar was at 1.5304 marks, up marginally.
Concern over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health contributed to a brief dollar rally overnight in Asia but the effects were short-lived after Moscow swiftly denied the president had died.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5304 marks and 111.47 yen compared with 1.5287 marks and 111.55 yen late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 2.2 points at 4007.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 11.21 at 2,135.50.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 16.35 at 2686.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $381.60 compared with $381.35 on Wednesday afternoon. Silver was three cents stronger at $4.97.
